source_caption:
One of the most disturbing moments in modern horror.

Hereditary (2018), written and directed by Ari Aster, is the kind of horror movie that gets under your skin without relying on cheap jump scares. It starts as a story about grief and a family falling apart after the death of their secretive grandmother, but slowly reveals something much darker hiding beneath it all.

Annie Graham, played by Toni Collette, begins uncovering disturbing secrets about her family’s past. As strange events take over the house, grief turns into paranoia, guilt and fear, and the Grahams find themselves trapped in a fate that seems to have been decided long before they were born.

Aster originally approached the film more like a family drama than a traditional horror movie, which is part of what makes it so uncomfortable. The horror comes from watching a family already struggling with trauma slowly collapse from the inside. 

The filmmaking is just as unsettling. Aster and cinematographer Pawel Pogorzelski deliberately gave the movie a dollhouse-like feeling. Much of the house was built on a soundstage, allowing the camera to move through the rooms with an almost miniature-like precision. Annie’s own miniature models mirror the real house, creating an eerie connection between the little worlds she builds and the world around her. 

And the miniatures were actually built at roughly 1:8 scale. The production had to carefully coordinate the miniature sets with the full-size sets so they could feel like exact versions of the same spaces. 

Toni Collette’s performance is another huge reason the movie works. She reportedly wasn’t even looking to make another heavy drama when she received the script, but felt she had to take the role after reading it. 

Made for around $10 million, Hereditary became Ari Aster’s feature-film debut and eventually grossed around $90 million worldwide. 

It’s not just a horror movie about a supernatural threat. It’s a movie about family trauma, grief and the terrifying possibility that some things are simply impossible to escape.

And that’s what makes it so disturbing.

source_details.synopsis: Hereditary is a 2018 American supernatural psychological horror film written and directed by Ari Aster in his feature directorial debut. Starring Toni Collette, Alex Wolff, Milly Shapiro, Ann Dowd, and Gabriel Byrne, the film follows Annie Graham (Collette), a grieving miniature artist who uncovers disturbing secrets about her recently deceased mother. She is subsequently tormented by sinister paranormal occurrences, along with her husband Steve (Byrne) and their children, Peter (Wolff) and Charlie (Shapiro).
